_doc: How the world's towns age visibly over the centuries (world/townEras.js; worlds made since terrainGen 8). A town passes through the architectural eras in order, never back: it takes the next once the world's year has reached the era's `from` (plus its culture's `shift`, plus a lag of 0..lagYears by a hash of the town, so neighbours don't all turn in one year) and its wealth score (world/settlementWealth.js) is at least `minScore` and it is at least `minType` (village < town < city < capital). Its history (settlement.townEra.history: [era, year, pace]) is filled back to the town's founding the first time it is seen, then advanced once a year (processDay). What an era builds: `tierCap` (the richest wealth tier its builders can raise: hearth folk build only as the poor do, mud and wattle under thatch, whatever their purse), `mix` (a ring of the culture's house mix that every house is drawn from in that era: 'edge' = huts, crofts and longhouses), `lamps` (none, square, or null = the culture's own), `paving` (which streets its masons lay, if the culture paves at all: main = the high street and square, lane = every lane; each spreads out from the square over `paveYears`), `walls` (what the town may ring itself with: palisade or stone). Each building stands in the style of the era it was last (re)built in: it lasts `life` years (by the era's materials, times the town's `pace` that era — a rich town renews faster, a poor one patches and makes do), its first build spread by a phase hashed from its district (a block of districtSize tiles, so a whole quarter is old together) and a little of its own. A building past `wear.worn` of its life is weathered (dulled, grimed, moss on its roof), past `wear.old` old (mossier, its roof sagging); then it is pulled down and rebuilt in the era of the day. `walls`: a town raises a palisade, later stone, when its type, wealth and the threats it faces allow — the chance each year is `chance` × (1 + threat), threat being its realm's wars, the sacks, fires and battles its memory holds, and an invasion abroad; stone walls are raised over a palisade, never the other way. `art`: the wall's materials by culture (scripts/make_town_walls.py composes assets/buildingKit/town_walls.png from the building kit's wall tiles and the street sheet's stone).

eras.label: the Hearth Age
eras.hint: wattle huts and longhouses under thatch, dirt tracks

eras.label: the Timber Age
eras.hint: timber halls, plaster and boards, shingle roofs

eras.label: the Age of Stone
eras.hint: stone houses, a cobbled high street, walls of stone

eras.label: the Guild Age
eras.hint: guildhalls and spires, every lane paved, lamps along the streets

cultures._doc: Years added to each era's `from` for a culture's towns (a people of stonemasons builds in stone sooner, forest folk later), by era id or `all`; `streets`: the paving a culture without its own (architecture.json plan.streets null) lays at last in the guild age — the high street and square only (a block of the street sheet).

pace._doc: How fast a town renews its houses in an era: life × (slow − (slow − fast) × its wealth score then), stamped on the era's history entry so it never shifts after.

notice.palisade: The folk of {town} ring their town with a palisade of sharpened stakes.
notice.stone: The folk of {town} raise a wall of stone about their town.

eraNotice.timber: In {town} the old huts give way to timber halls and plastered houses.
eraNotice.stone: {town} is building in stone now: masons from afar, and the high street cobbled.
eraNotice.guild: {town} has come into its own: guildhalls, spires, and every lane paved.

spires._doc: A Guild Age town's church, temple, guildhall or town hall raises a belltower over its roof (era `spires`): 2 cells wide and 5 tall, composed by scripts/make_town_walls.py into this sheet from the kit's walls, roof tiles and bell emblem, in this order; drawn by ui/buildingWear.js over the middle of the building's ridge.

art._doc: Materials, each a band of rows in the sheet (scripts/make_town_walls.py): `face` the building kit wall the face is cut from, `cap` the street sheet block the wall walk is paved with (stone) or null (a palisade: stake tops). Cultures pick theirs by kind.
